transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I've been having a really hard time focusing and paying attention to details lately. I keep making careless mistakes at work that I normally shouldn't be making, and it's starting to really worry me.
How long have you been having these concentration and careless-mistake problems, and did they start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

They've been particularly bad for about a year and five months, but I've actually had these issues since I was a child, well before age 12. I don't recall them starting after any specific stressful event or major life change.
Do you also have problems with hyperactivity or impulsivity, such as feeling restless, fidgeting, interrupting others, or acting before thinking?

No, I don't really experience things like restlessness, fidgeting, or acting before thinking. My struggles are definitely much more about my focus, attention, and making those careless mistakes I mentioned.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, such as at work, at home, or in school, and do they interfere with your daily functioning?

To be honest, I'm not really sure and haven't thought about it in that way. I've mostly just been focusing on how much it's affecting my work lately, so I haven't paid as much attention to other areas of my life.
Before age 12, did teachers or family members also notice that you were forgetful, easily distracted, or had trouble finishing tasks at home or school?

Yes, they definitely did. My elementary school teachers constantly wrote on my report cards that I was easily distracted and always losing my homework or pencils. My parents also used to get quite frustrated with me for constantly misplacing my things around the house.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, such as at work, at home, or in school, and do they interfere with your daily functioning?

Like I said, I'm really not sure and haven't thought much about how it affects other areas. I've mostly just been focused on the mistakes I'm making at my job, so I haven't paid much attention to how it impacts my home life.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was ADHD, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation, and that remains the best fit. The history strongly supports childhood-onset inattention before age 12, with persistent distractibility, losing items, and careless mistakes. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are denied, making the combined or hyperactive/impulsive presentations unlikely. There is no evidence of a mood, psychotic, anxiety, trauma-related, or stress-related syndrome driving the symptoms, so the differential has not expanded.
